title: Backend Engineer - Agentic AI (m/w/d)
description:
Overview

getpress entwickelt eine eigene KI-Agenten-Plattform (LangGraph, PostgreSQL, Next.js) für die PR-Branche


Der Servicemarkt, von Legal über Consulting bis hin zu Agenturen, steht vor der größten Transformation der Geschichte. Gleichzeitig wird der milliardenschwere PR-Markt im Zeitalter von AI-Visibility gerade immer wichtiger. getpress, eine der am schnellsten wachsenden PR-Agenturen Deutschlands (>40 Leute, Kund*innen wie Trivago, Komoot, Fonio AI oder AutoScout24), hat sich entschieden, diesen Wandel zu führen statt abzuwarten. Wir bauen die PR Company der Zukunft: keine reine Service-Company mehr, sondern eine Service-as-a-Software-Company. 


Unser AI-Team besteht nun seit 4 Monaten, aktuell ein Developer, eine Produktmanagerin und unsere Head of AI. Die Grundarchitektur steht, erste Teile unserer PR-Plattform und des Multi-Agent-Systems laufen produktiv. Jetzt fehlst du – die Person, die als Backend Engineer das technische Fundament zusammen mit unserem zweiten Developer ownt und gemeinsam neu definiert, wie die PR der Zukunft funktioniert.


Deine Rolle

  • PR-Plattform: Fullstack-Entwicklung der Plattform, die das Operating System der PR-Agentur 2027 wird. Nah an den Nutzer*innen, in schnellen Entwicklungszyklen, und wo deine Entscheidungen den Kurs setzen.

  • KI-Agenten: Aufbau eines Agenten-Systems, das die PR-Wertschöpfungskette End-to-End neu definiert. Du baust die Agenten, mit denen unsere Berater*innen täglich arbeiten, inkl. Self-Learning-Loops und Multi-Agent-Orchestrierung.

  • Systemarchitektur: Mitgestalten der Systemarchitektur, inkl. Workflows, Datenmodell, Schnittstellen, Compliance und Tech Stack (bisher vorwiegend PostgreSQL, Next.js, LangGraph, Docker)

  • Datenmanagement: Weiterentwicklung der Datenbank-Architektur inkl. relationaler Daten- und Vektor-Datenbanken


Wer du bist

Must haves:

  • > 3 Jahre Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung

  • > 1 Jahr Erfahrung in der Entwicklung von KI-Agenten und -Komponenten wie Memory, Context-Engineering, Retrieval und Orchestration unter Verwendung von Frameworks wie Langchain, CrewAI, Langgraph o.ä.

  • Tech Stack: TypeScript, Python, PostgreSQL, Docker, Git, LangGraph, Github

  • Erfahrung in der Entwicklung von Backend-Systemen mit Frameworks (fastAPI, springboot, nestJS, etc.) und gängigen Programmiersprachen (z.B. Java, Typescript, Python)

  • Erfahrung mit Container-based und Cloud-native Architekturen (Docker, Kubernetes, AWS oder ähnlich)

  • C1-Deutschkenntnisse sind von Vorteil, B2-Niveau ist ausreichend (mit Motivation in deinem ersten Arbeitsjahr den Kurs zu C1 zu machen)

Nice to haves:

  • Datenkompetenz: Sicher in SQL, API Design, Schema-Design, Query Optimization

  • Erfahrung mit der Integration von KI-/ML-Modellen in Produktionssysteme, sowie im Verständnis des Modellverhaltens, der Modellleistung und der Modellbeschränkungen

  • Product-Engineering: Erfahrung darin, Anforderungen aus Business- und Nutzer:innen-Perspektive einzuordnen, bevor sie technisch umgesetzt werden

  • Erfahrung in Event-Driven Architecture (Kafka, RabbitMQ, o.ä.)

  • Erfahrung mit Agentic Development (Claude Code, Codex, o.ä.)


Was dich erwartet

  • Architekt des Tech-Layers: Du bist unser technischer Experte und gestaltest mit, wie getpress Technologie denkt und nutzt

  • KI in Anwendung: Du bringst KI an der Vorfront technischer Möglichkeiten in unsere Prozesse und Strategie

  • Autonomie: Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Management, setzt eigene Ideen um und definierst Standards, an denen wir uns orientieren

  • Ein echtes Team: Wir begegnen einander auf Augenhöhe – offen, ehrlich und mit echtem Interesse am Gegenüber. Wir lernen voneinander, geben einander Rückhalt und feiern gemeinsame Erfolge.

  • Flexibilität, die wirklich gelebt wird: Ob im Berliner Office oder remote (in DE) – wir setzen auf flexible Arbeitsmodelle mit viel Eigenverantwortung. Wir suchen jemanden mit Wohnsitz in Deutschland. Das heißt wann und wo (in DE) du deinen Arbeitsalltag gestaltest, entscheidest du selbst. Klare Kommunikation und Vertrauen sind dabei für uns selbstverständlich.

title: Mechanical Engineer in Production [Mid-Senior; F/M/D]
description:
Your mission

If you're a mechanical engineer and want to apply your skills to food production technology, this is your chance to develop innovative mechanical systems for plant-based meat manufacturing, this is your chance to take the next step and take operational responsibility. Join us now as we scale operations in a fast-growing, purpose-driven startup.

Key responsibilities

  • Machinery Installation & Commissioning: Support installation of new food processing equipment, perform commissioning and validation procedures, and conduct functional testing to ensure proper operation before production use.

  • Continuous Modification & Improvement: Analyze existing processes and equipment performance, identify improvements, and design modifications to increase efficiency, reliability, and food safety compliance. Implement optimizations in the production environment.

  • Equipment Repair & Troubleshooting: Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, integrated and pneumatic equipment failures. Troubleshoot complex issues in mixers, conveyors, industrial machines, and automation equipment. Implement timely repairs to minimize production downtime.

  • Mechanical Design & Process Optimization: Build and test mechanical prototypes and  operational processes, validate design performance through testing and prototyping, iterate designs based on production feedback and food safety requirements.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with production, R&D and quality teams to optimize equipment performance and resolve complex production challenges. Communicate equipment status and maintenance needs to production planning and leadership.

  • Technical documentation: Develop and maintain comprehensive technical documentation including S.O.P.s, schematics, mechanical drawings, process diagrams, and system specifications.

  • Vendor & Contractor Management: Manage relationships with external vendors, contractors, and service providers. Coordinate procurement activities, oversee contractor performance, and ensure project deliverables meet specifications.



Your profile

In this role, you'll be responsible for designing custom food processing equipment, developing mechanical solutions for plant-based protein manufacturing, and supporting the mechanical engineering needs of our production operations. As a hands-on mechanical engineer, you'll work on everything from equipment design to production support.

Requirements

  • Professional Experience: 5-8 years of mechanical engineering experience in production or manufacturing environment, preferably with exposure to food processing, manufacturing equipment, or automated systems.

  • Educational Background: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related technical field. Strong foundation in equipment maintenance, reliability engineering, and manufacturing processes. Knowledge of food industry applications preferred.

  • Technical Skills: Knowledge of manufacturing processes and production optimization techniques, familiarity with lean manufacturing principles. Strong troubleshooting abilities with hands-on experience developing mechanical solutions and diagnosing and repairing mechanical equipment failures. Proficiency with CAD software, process modeling tools, and manufacturing software systems.

  • Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with experience in root cause analysis and process troubleshooting. Ability to interpret production data and develop longlasting cost effective engineering solutions.

title: Senior Solutions Consultant (m/f/d) - Growth & Strategy
description:
The Role

This is a senior role combining consulting, technology and commercial responsibility. You’ll work directly with customers to understand their processes and challenges, then turn those requirements into practical Smartsheet solutions. You’ll build and present proof of concepts, scope consulting projects, discuss pricing and ultimately help win the work.
You’ll play an important role in AMX’s continued growth, with an initial focus on the DACH market. You’ll work with opportunities from Smartsheet, our partner network and existing customers, while also helping develop new relationships over time. The focus is on building trust, understanding where AMX can add value and turning strong customer relationships into sustainable growth.
There’s also real scope for this role to grow. With proven success, you’ll take on broader responsibility for how AMX develops opportunities and goes to market, initially through greater ownership of customers, regions and commercial strategy. Over time, this can also develop into mentoring and guiding the team as it grows.What You’ll Be Doing

  • Manage customer opportunities end-to-end, from discovery and requirements gathering through solution design, proof of concepts, scoping, pricing and commercial discussions, before handing over to the implementation team.
  • Build strong relationships with existing customers, identifying new use cases and opportunities to expand successful solutions across other teams, departments and markets.
  • Work closely with Smartsheet Account Executives and the wider Smartsheet team on joint account planning, developing opportunities and identifying growth accounts across DACH and AMX’s wider markets.
  • Help develop new opportunities through targeted account research, strategic outreach, events and collaboration with AMX’s marketing and partner network.
  • Contribute to and help shape AMX’s wider consulting and commercial approach, including how we develop opportunities, work with partners and take solutions to market.
  • As you progress, mentor other consultants and take on increasing responsibility across AMX’s commercial activities.


Your profile

  • You have strong experience in technology consulting, solutions consulting, SaaS or digital transformation.
  • You’re commercially minded and comfortable taking a customer conversation from discovery through solution design, scoping, negotiation and close.
  • You’re equally technically hands-on and comfortable actually building and demonstrating what you propose. Smartsheet experience is a big advantage, but strong Excel skills or experience configuring SaaS, workflow, low-code or business applications can also be a great fit.
  • You’re good at asking the right questions and turning complex or unclear business problems into structured solutions.
  • You’re confident presenting to senior stakeholders and can explain technical solutions in terms of business value.
  • You enjoy building customer relationships and spotting new opportunities.
  • You’re comfortable working without a perfect playbook. You like bringing your own ideas, testing what works and helping shape the processes and approach that will make AMX successful as we grow.
  • You’re interested in growing beyond an individual contributor role, mentoring others and taking on broader responsibility over time.
  • You speak German at native/C2 level and English fluently.
  • You’re ideally based in Germany and comfortable travelling for customers, partner meetings and events, typically up to five days per month.
  • A relevant degree is welcome, but your experience and what you’ve actually delivered are much more important to us.


Why us?

  • You’ll join an established and successful consultancy that is still small enough for you to have a real influence on how things are done.
  • You’ll have genuine flexibility around where you work, with a remote-first setup and only occasional travel for customers, partner meetings and team events.
  • The role comes with a strong fixed salary, with regular salary reviews as your responsibilities and seniority grow.
  • You’ll receive a €3,000 annual learning and development budget, home-office support, a flexible €50 monthly benefits allowance, wellness and technology allowances and regular team retreats.
  • You won’t simply be executing somebody else’s playbook. You’ll have the freedom to bring your own ideas, shape how we work and help define what successful growth looks like.
  • Most importantly, there’s room for this to become much more than a typical Senior Consultant position. If things go well, we want you to take on broader commercial responsibility, help develop the team and play an important role in AMX’s continued growth across DACH and beyond.

title: Business Development / Mba Co-Founder (F/M/D) Role At Startup Chillquanta
description:
**CHILLQUANTA
**Bochum, Germany (Ruhr University Bochum) | On-site / Hybrid | Co-Founder / Equity | Deep Tech / Quantum & Semiconductor Metrology

**About ChillQuanta
**ChillQuanta is developing an electro-optic spectrometer for inspecting and characterizing photonic qubits (semiconductor quantum-dot single- and entangled-photon sources), aiming to replace or combine today's separate methods (capacitance-voltage, photoluminescence, resonance fluorescence spectroscopy) with one new sub-100-femtosecond-resolution, non-destructive electro-optic technique — with a patent filing already in progress. Target market: quantum and semiconductor chip makers.

**The opportunity
**Founded by Amar Alok (CEO, PhD in Experimental Physics from RUB, 4+ years in ultrafast optics and pump-probe spectroscopy) alongside a Chemistry postdoc, ChillQuanta has a lab prototype (TRL 3-4) benchmarked against single-atom data, an Invention Disclosure accepted by RUB (April 2026) with a manuscript in preparation for Physical Review Letters, and over €12k raised so far. The next step is turning the lab prototype into an automated instrument and deciding between licensing and starting a company — which is where a business co-founder comes in. ChillQuanta is separately also open to an AI/ML co-founder to help build wafer-scale AI prediction capability.

Tasks

What you will own

**Company build-up & strategy
**- Help decide and execute the path from lab prototype to company: licensing vs. start-up, incorporation, and go-to-market strategy for the quantum/semiconductor metrology market.
- Own fundraising strategy and investor relations as ChillQuanta moves beyond its initial ~€12k raised.

**Commercialization
**- Turn the lab prototype (TRL 3-4) into an automated, sellable instrument in partnership with the technical team.
- Build relationships with semiconductor and quantum chip makers as early customers and design partners.
Business operations
- Establish the commercial and operational foundation (pricing, business model, partnerships) the founding science team doesn't yet have.

Requirements

**What you bring
**

**Core experience
**- Business development or MBA-level commercial experience, ideally with deep-tech, scientific instrumentation, or semiconductor/quantum industry exposure.
- Comfort making a licensing-vs-startup call and building a go-to-market plan from a lab-stage prototype.

**Especially valuable
**- Existing network in quantum technology, semiconductor metrology, or scientific instrumentation.
- Fundraising experience for deep-tech ventures (grants and/or investors).
- ChillQuanta is separately seeking an AI/ML co-founder to build wafer-scale AI prediction — relevant ML/software experience is valuable for that parallel track.

Benefits

Why join ChillQuanta
- A validated lab prototype (TRL 3-4) benchmarked against single-atom data, with an Invention Disclosure already accepted by RUB and a manuscript heading to Physical Review Letters.
- A genuinely novel technique (patent filing in progress) addressing a real gap in photonic-qubit inspection for the fast-growing quantum and semiconductor chip markets.
- Ground-floor business co-founder equity alongside a strong physics/chemistry founding team.

ChillQuanta welcomes co-founder candidates regardless of gender, age, ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, sexual identity, or any other characteristic. This is a search for the right partner to build the company with, not a conventional hire.

title: Senior Technical Support Engineer
Senior Software Engineer New Markets - EU
Senior Customer Enablement Manager (London, United Kingdom)
Product Business Analyst
description:
About us

SFG20 is the industry standard for building maintenance. Providing services and pioneering technologies that empower people to create and sustain safer buildings.

Our mission is to make buildings better using our standard, software and expertise. Our vision is to become the leading authority for built environment maintenance that protects and enhances quality of life.

About the role

The Product Business Analyst bridges the gap between business needs and engineering delivery, turning ideas, requests and requirements into clear, actionable work.

By bringing clarity to ambiguity, connecting work across Product and Platform Engineering and making sure teams have the information they need, the role helps reduce rework, improve delivery and build better software for our customers.

Key Responsibilities

Discovery and shaping

  • Work with stakeholders to explore ideas, requests and feedback, clarifying the underlying problem, business need and intended outcome before work is defined

  • Explore the reasons behind requests before work is defined, ensuring relevant context and requirements are understood.

  • Challenge assumptions constructively, identify gaps and surface conflicting needs or unanswered questions early.

  • Identify and engage the right stakeholders to provide the information and decisions needed to shape clear requirements.

Turning needs into actionable work

  • Translate business needs into clear epics, features, user stories and acceptance criteria that give engineering teams sufficient context to progress work effectively.

  • Break down defined or moderately complex initiatives into clear, deliverable increments, working with Product and Engineering colleagues and seeking support on more complex work where needed,

  • Maintain accurate requirements and supporting context in Jira, including agreed scope, relevant decisions and material changes.

  • Keep requirements current as understanding or scope develops, working with relevant Product, Engineering and project colleagues to capture what has changed and why.

Question resolution during delivery

  • Remain closely involved during delivery as a point of contact for requirements-related questions and clarification.

  • Investigate ambiguity, work with the right stakeholders to resolve requirements questions and escalate more complex issues where needed so engineering teams can continue with clear direction.

  • Participate in refinement and planning discussions where business analysis input is needed to clarify scope, requirements or agreed decisions.

  • Maintain traceability from the original business need through agreed requirements and material changes to what is ultimately delivered.

Integrating product and platform work

  • Maintain awareness of relevant work across Product and Platform Engineering and identify dependencies, overlaps or potential impacts between teams.

  • Help shape requirements where product and platform changes need to work together, ensuring relevant dependencies and constraints are understood.

  • Flag where teams may be addressing the same problem, where proposed changes could conflict, or where work in one area creates an impact elsewhere.

  • Support effective handovers and cross-team working by ensuring teams have the requirements context and documentation they need.

Stakeholder engagement

  • Build constructive working relationships across Product, Engineering, QA, customer-facing teams and the wider business.

  • Translate engineering questions and constraints into clear language for business stakeholders.

  • Translate business needs and agreed intent into precise, actionable requirements for engineering teams.

  • Help stakeholders understand what has been agreed from a requirements perspective, what remains unresolved and where further input or decisions are needed.

Essential experience

  • Proven experience as a Business Analyst, or in a closely related analysis role, within software delivery.

  • Strong requirements elicitation and analysis skills, including the ability to work from incomplete or ambiguous information, identify gaps and challenge assumptions constructively.

  • Ability to translate business needs into clear, structured requirements, including epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria and supporting documentation.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage stakeholders at all levels and follow through to obtain the information needed to resolve ambiguity.

  • Experience working with Jira and Agile software delivery teams.

  • Experience working across multiple teams where shared dependencies, changes or overlapping requirements need to be understood clearly.

  • A good level of technical understanding, enabling effective conversations with engineers about scope, constraints, dependencies and trade-offs.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with good attention to detail and the ability to maintain clarity as requirements evolve.

Desirable experience

  • Experience working in a SaaS or platform engineering environment.

  • Familiarity with APIs, integrations and how platform capabilities can underpin product features.

  • Experience using analysis techniques such as process mapping or user journey mapping.

  • Exposure to software release processes and change management.

Additional Information

All candidates must be able to demonstrate a pre-existing right to work and travel within the UK. We are unfortunately not able to offer sponsorship. Documentary evidence will be required.

All offers are subject to satisfactory vetting and reference checks.

title: Strategic Account Manager - London
description:
Meet Siena

Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.

It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.

The team

We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.

We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.

If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.

The Role

You own the commercial relationship for Siena's highest-value brands: renewals, expansion, executive trust, and knowing your accounts better than anyone. A deployment strategist owns product outcomes for the same accounts, and together you're the Siena pod.

You're accountable for net dollar retention, expansion quota attainment, and executive relationship health across your book. You own our Growth and Strategic segment accounts, not the full customer book, working at the intersection of customer, sales, and your deployment strategist. Expect moderate travel for in-person workshops, account visits, and QBRs.

What You'll Do

  • Own the commercial relationship end to end for a portfolio of Growth and Strategic accounts, from post-onboarding through long-term growth: build concrete account plans, track impact with data, and hold customers and internal teams accountable when progress stalls

  • Map every account and build executive trust: maintain a living stakeholder map, build relationships with decision-makers beyond day-to-day contacts, and own the executive cadence so leadership sees Siena's value before renewal conversations start

  • Drive commercial outcomes: own renewal negotiations, independently identify and close expansion opportunities, and quantify customer ROI in cost savings, efficiency, or revenue impact

  • Bring product depth to the relationship: understand how Siena's agents work together, explain capabilities confidently, and guide customers on the best strategic use cases

  • Lead cross-functional execution: turn vague customer problems into clear problem statements and execution plans, partnering with other teams as needed

Who You Are

The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you.

  • 3+ years in account management with technical, complex software, including at least one independently negotiated $100k+ deal

  • Startup background: comfortable in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, wearing many hats

  • E-commerce or CX industry experience: customers respond better to AMs who speak their language

Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one.

  • Hands-on AI experience: you've built an agent, automated a workflow, or created a tool, not just used ChatGPT for email

  • Enterprise experience: managed complex orgs, sold to multiple stakeholders

  • Close collaboration experience with product and engineering teams

  • Self-directed: brings solutions, not just problems

  • Balances empathy with commercial impact, willing to challenge the status quo when it blocks results

Nice to Have: Bonus, not required.

  • Experience at a native AI technology company

  • Comfort with API integrations, conversation flow design, and business intelligence tools

Not a Fit If:

  • You want a fixed playbook and clear SOPs before you start

  • You'd rather support the commercial conversation than own it

  • You need close oversight rather than working independently with your deployment strategist as your main partner

Why Siena?

Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.

Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.

A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.

Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.

Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.

AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.

Our values

The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.

They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.

Our approach to AI

The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.

Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.

At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.

How we hire

We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at Siena provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $100B in annualized spend flows in and out of 50,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

 

About the Role

Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

  • Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

  • Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

  • Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

  • Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

  • Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

What You Need

  • You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

  • You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

  • You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

  • You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

  • You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

  • You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

  • You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

  • You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

  • Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

  • Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

  • Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

Why be a CX Associates at Ramp

  • Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

  • AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

  • Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

  • Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.

Read more about how Ramp thinks about AI and CX:

  • How Ramp Became an AI-First Company — Geoff Charles, CPO

  • Inside Glass: How Ramp Built a Proprietary AI Platform for CX — Seb Goddijn, AI Product Manager

  • AI-Powered Customer Experience at Ramp — Ben Levick, Head of CX / Ramp AI

What to know before you apply

  • Schedule & Shift Bidding - Please Read Carefully: This role is part of Ramp’s UK-based overnight coverage strategy. Team members will work a set 40-hour/week schedule designed to support customer needs outside US business hours. Schedules may include evenings, weekends, and rotating holiday coverage, depending on business needs.

  • Hours Expected: CX Associates work a set 40-hour/week schedule assigned through a schedule-bid process. Work shifts will span between 6:30 AM–3:30 PM BST, and your shift will likely include a weekend day (either Sun–Thu or Tues-Sat). Associates also cover 2–3 company holidays per year on a rotating basis. Ramp's customers operate on financial deadlines that don't pause.

  • This is a fast-changing environment: Ramp’s product and customer needs evolve quickly. Success in this role requires comfort with ambiguity, strong judgment, and a willingness to learn new systems, workflows, and product surfaces continuously.

  • You’ll help build this function: This is not just a support role within an existing system. This team is being built as part of Ramp’s broader international CX strategy, so strong operators will have the opportunity to shape processes, team culture, and how overnight coverage works as the function scales.

  • This role is a launchpad for your career at one of the fastest-growing companies in fintech.

Right to Work: All candidates must have the right to work in the United Kingdom. We will require evidence of your right to work as part of the recruitment process in accordance with the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006.

 

For candidates located in the UK, the pay range for this role is £39,000-£43,000 per year.

title: Sales Manager, Enterprise
description:
Why Rogo

Our mission is to transform global finance by empowering professionals at the world's top investment banks, private equity funds, and investment firms with AI that delivers unparalleled speed, accuracy, and insight. We're not just improving financial workflows; we're redefining them.

This is a unique opportunity to join a generational company driving transformation in one of the most important industries in the world. With a rapidly growing, global client base, proven product-market fit, and backing from world-class investors, we are scaling quickly and defining a new category of enterprise AI.

Our team is sharp, motivated, and deeply committed to Rogo’s mission. We take ownership of complex problems and stay relentlessly focused on our users. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, demand excellence, and want to help build the future of finance, we invite you to join us.

What You Will Own

  • Build, lead, and coach a team of enterprise account executives selling into global banks, PE firms, and asset managers.

  • Own team-level new-logo and expansion ARR targets, and personally engage in strategic deals as a player-coach when needed.

  • Recruit, hire, and ramp top enterprise sales talent as the team scales.

  • Instill rigorous forecasting, pipeline hygiene, and deal execution discipline using MEDDPICC.

  • Partner with RevOps, Marketing, and Post-Sales to build repeatable, scalable go-to-market motions.

  • Coach reps on multi-threading, executive engagement, and navigating complex enterprise procurement, security, and legal cycles.

  • Represent the enterprise segment in leadership forecast reviews and strategic planning.

What You Will Need

7+ years in enterprise SaaS sales, including 3+ years directly managing a quota-carrying AE team.

  • Track record of building and leading teams that consistently exceed $1M+ individual quotas.

  • Deep fluency in MEDDPICC or Command of the Message, with experience installing sales methodology across a team.

  • Experience hiring, onboarding, and developing enterprise sellers.

  • Ability to operate as both a strategic leader and a hands-on coach in live deal cycles.

  • Comfortable operating in a fast-scaling startup environment with evolving process and ambiguity.

Bonus

  • Experience selling to investment banks, PE, or capital-markets teams.

  • Experience scaling a sales team to 10+ reps.

  • Familiarity with LLMs, data-privacy standards, and enterprise infosec reviews.

Who You Are

  • You thrive in fast-paced environments. You are high-intensity and care a lot about what you do, and you're ecstatic to work at a startup.

  • You are ambitious. You have fun solving problems that others think are impossible.

  • You are curious. You find joy in learning about AI, technology, and finance.

  • You are an owner. You are autonomous, self-directed, and comfortable working with ambiguity.

  • You are collaborative, organized, thoughtful, and kind.

Why Join Rogo?

  • Up and to the right: Rogo has strong product adoption with the world's leading financial institutions, and we are still early. The upside is enormous.

  • Extraordinary team: we take talent density seriously. You'll do the best work of your career alongside some of the sharpest people in AI and finance.

  • A one-of-one problem: bringing AI to the core of how Wall Street works is one of the most ambitious, technically demanding, and consequential problems today. There is nowhere else you can work on it at this scale.

  • Real ownership: You'll own real surface area and watch the world's most sophisticated users rely on your work.

  • Always at the frontier: we work at the edge of what the best models can do and turn it into products people trust. If you're obsessed with AI, this is where it's happening.

title: Director, Social Media & Technical Communications
description:
About Radiant

Radiant is looking for a senior social media and communications leader who can turn deep technical substance into public narrative, executive voice and market momentum.

The right candidate is a high-agency B2B technology storyteller: technically curious, editorially sharp, deeply fluent in social media, and resourceful enough to build a steady pipeline of speaking opportunities, conference submissions, podcast pitches, panels, awards, and executive visibility moments.

You should be comfortable operating in complex technical markets AI infrastructure, GPUs, datacenters, developer platforms, enterprise software or similar categories. You do not need to be an engineer, but you need to be able to sit with technical leaders, understand what matters, find the angle, and translate it into language that is sharp, credible, and useful.

What You’ll Own

Social Media Strategy & Execution

You will own the company’s social presence across executive and corporate channels, with a particular focus on LinkedIn and other platforms where technical buyers, partners, investors, customers, and industry influencers spend time.

You will develop the strategy, write the content, shape the voice, test formats, track performance, and build a social engine that is sharp, intelligent, and distinctive. This includes company posts, executive posts, technical POVs, event coverage, launch support, partner amplification, customer moments, recruiting content, and timely commentary on industry developments.

Executive Voice & Thought Leadership

You will help build and sharpen the public voices of the company’s executives and technical leaders. That means developing points of view, ghostwriting posts, preparing talking points, identifying timely angles, and turning internal conviction into external narrative.

Technical Communications

You will work closely with product marketing, product, engineering, infrastructure, sales, partnerships and leadership to understand what the company is building and why it matters.

You will translate technical topics into clear, compelling communications for the market. This may include short-form social content, executive posts, speaking abstracts, event messaging, award submissions, customer stories, and thought-leadership themes.

You should know how to ask good questions, pressure-test claims, avoid hype, and make technical content accessible without making it shallow.

Speaking, Awards & Opportunity Pipeline

You will build and manage a proactive speaking and visibility engine for the company and its executives.

We expect a consistent weekly motion: sourcing opportunities, drafting abstracts, preparing submissions, pitching panels, finding podcasts, tracking deadlines, managing speaker assets, and creating a calendar of external visibility opportunities.

The expectation is not that every submission turns into a talk. The expectation is that the opportunity pipeline is always moving.

Tools, Analytics & Leverage

You should be fluent with modern marketing, social, research, writing, analytics, AI, design, video, transcript, and workflow tools. We are looking for someone who uses tools to move faster, test more ideas, repurpose better, and increase output quality without adding process drag. You should be comfortable measuring what works, identifying patterns, and improving the system over time.

Who You Are

You have 7–10+ years of experience in B2B technology communications, social media, content, executive communications, PR, thought leadership, or a closely related function.

You have worked in technical markets and can show that you understand how to communicate complex products, platforms, or infrastructure to sophisticated audiences.

You are an exceptional writer with strong editorial judgment.

You are social-native, not social-adjacent. You understand hooks, formats, timing, voice, audience behavior, and what makes technical content travel.

You are deeply resourceful. You do not wait to be handed opportunities. You find them, qualify them, pursue them, and keep the machine moving.

You are creative with language, formats, and tools.

You are commercially aware. You understand that social and communications should support brand, category creation, executive visibility, partner credibility, recruiting, customer confidence, and pipeline influence.

You are highly autonomous. You need direction, context, and access - not constant supervision.

Ideal Background

The strongest candidates may come from high-growth B2B technology companies, AI infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, developer tools, data infrastructure, enterprise software, telecom, semiconductors, or technical agencies with deep B2B experience.

Agency experience can be valuable if you have been hands-on with technical storytelling and executive communications. Big-company experience can be valuable if you have also operated with startup speed and ownership.

What matters most is quality of output, technical curiosity, taste, velocity, and judgment.

This Role Is Not

  • This is not a maintenance role.

  • This is not a role for someone who only manages calendars, routes approvals, or posts pre-written updates.

  • This is not a traditional PR role or media relations role.

  • This is not a generic social media role focused on lightweight engagement.

  • We are looking for someone who can build a communications engine around a complex technical company - someone who can find the story, sharpen the point of view, create the content, and push the company into the right conversations.

Why should you join us?

 

What sets us apart is our blend of modern technology, competitive benefits, and an open, welcoming work culture that enables our people to thrive.

 

Here are just some of the great things you can expect from us:

  • 25 days of annual leave

  • A culture that emphasises results over hierarchy, process & ego: we place great emphasis on the quality, ingenuity and creativity of work.

  • Open communication, regular feedback: we value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and a growth mindset makes us better together.

  • Learning Time: we all have dedicated learning time to focus on new skills, projects or interests that lay outside of your day-to-day job.

  • Health & Wellbeing: we want everyone to feel healthy and happy, so we offer private medical insurance via Bupa.

  • Cycle to Work Scheme: we're committed to building a sustainable business, so we encourage cycling to work.

  • Gympass subscription to a variety of gyms and wellbeing apps

  • Participation in the company shares program

  • Enhanced parental pay & leave

Diversity, Equality, Inclusion and Belonging

We are an equal opportunity employer and we strive to reduce unconscious bias throughout our hiring process. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran, neurodiversity status or disability status. To ensure our recruitment processes provide an equal opportunity for all applicants to succeed, we encourage you to let us know if there are any adjustments that we can make.

title: Performance & Development Lead (Fractional)
description:
About the role

This role is about performance development, not performance management. Unity's approach to performance is built on genuine ownership and accountability, not a traditional annual review cycle — but the system itself isn't the point. The point is helping people actually grow into what that ownership requires: sharper judgement, stronger client and commercial instincts, real skill in giving and using feedback, and the behaviours that take someone from new joiner to trusted senior contributor.

This role exists to build that growth, not to run the administrative mechanics of reviews and calibration. It's about coaching Partners and Functional Leaders to develop their people well, giving every new joiner a genuine development runway from day one, and building the skills, frameworks and programmes that help people grow faster and more deliberately than they would simply by doing the job. Classic L&D sits inside this, but the mandate is bigger: making sure people are developing, not just being assessed.

What you'll own

  • Feedback and check-in skills: build the skills behind how Unity gives and receives feedback — people requesting feedback proactively, managers giving sharp and timely feedback, and check-in conversations that are genuinely structured performance discussions, not informal catch-ups

  • Learning programmes: design and curate the professional and technical skills development that sits underneath the performance model — practical, tied to real work, sourcing external providers where that's the better route and building internal content where it isn't

  • Calibration and promotion readiness: help Partners and Functional Leaders build strong evidence for promotion and reward decisions — coaching on what good evidence looks like, so panels can make fair, consistent, well-evidenced decisions

  • Probation and onboarding: own onboarding and the probation experience so new joiners and their sponsors get real substance from day one, with every new hire set up to demonstrate strong early contribution

  • Performance tooling literacy: build firm-wide understanding of the modern performance tools Unity uses to connect strategy to individual accountability, so they build trust rather than anxiety

  • Skills and progression frameworks: define skills and progression frameworks for client-facing and enablement tracks that map onto Unity's own grading and progression criteria, working with the Reward Lead so learning pathways line up with progression and pay

  • Measurement: use data, not just attendance or completion rates, to track whether this work is actually changing behaviour — feedback quality, check-in substance, calibration consistency — and report to the CPO and Management Team

What success looks like in year one

  • Partners and Functional Leaders visibly more confident and skilled at developing their people, not just assessing them

  • People growing faster and more deliberately, with real development evidence behind every promotion case, not last-minute case-building

  • Every new joiner on a genuine development runway from day one, not just surviving probation

  • A live, skills-based framework that people can see their own growth against

What we're looking for

  • Senior experience in people development, performance coaching or L&D, ideally somewhere with a strong, explicit growth philosophy rather than a generic annual-review cycle

  • Genuine comfort connecting development work to how Unity assesses and rewards performance, without this becoming a process-administration role

  • A strong instructional designer and facilitator — able to build and personally deliver programmes, not only commission them

  • Energised by growing people and building a development mindset into how they work, rather than running review mechanics or delivering content for its own sake

  • A pragmatic prioritiser, comfortable scoping ambitious work into 3 focused days a week and sequencing what matters most first

  • Confident coaching senior Partners and Directors on how to develop their people, not just how to assess them

How this role fits at Unity

You'll sit in the People Team working with the Chief People Officer, the Reward Lead, and People Ops, and work closely with Partners and Functional Leaders across client teams and enablement teams. Feedback, check-ins, probation and calibration are where your impact shows up, but the goal is always growth, not process — this isn't a separate, bolt-on training function.

title: AI Enablement Lead
description:
About the role

This role exists to make sure everybody at Unity — every Partner and Functional Leader, and everyone in their teams — can actually use AI well in their everyday work, and to turn that capability into real automation and productivity gains across the business. It reports jointly to the Chief People Officer and the Chief AI Officer, because doing this well is as much about people, capability and how Unity actually works day to day as it is about the technology itself.

It suits someone who lives at the frontier of what's possible with AI — building with the latest tools themselves and evolving their own approach every few weeks, not working from a playbook that's a year out of date. It suits someone who gets real satisfaction from building capability in others, reimagining how work actually gets done, and shipping things that stick, rather than setting technology direction from the top. You'll be building the operational muscle of Unity's AI Centre of Excellence from scratch, and sequencing what matters most first.

What you'll own

  • Firm-wide AI capability and training: design and drive practical AI upskilling across client-facing and enablement teams, working closely with the Performance & Development Lead so AI capability is built into onboarding and ongoing development, not run as a separate initiative

  • Reimagining the work: spot where new AI capability means Unity can remove whole steps or approach a problem completely differently, not just automate what already exists, then get alongside client teams and enablement functions to make it real

  • Automation and adoption: identify, prioritise and deliver automation that maximises the value Unity gets from the AI tools already in use, and evaluate new ones on their merits

  • Role and ways-of-working design: as AI takes on more of the work, help Unity rethink who does what, where judgement sits and how junior people learn — including, as whole workflows move onto Weaver, designing the team and role changes that follow: new responsibilities around workflow ownership, supervision, judgement and exceptions

  • Governance in practice: implement the policies and guardrails the Chief AI Officer sets for safe, compliant and ethical AI use — covering data privacy and client confidentiality — making sure they're followed in practice without slowing teams down

  • Build, ship and partner with Engineering: personally build and ship smaller tools and prototypes using the latest AI capabilities; bring in VP Product and Engineering when something needs shared integrations, scaling or ongoing production support

  • Tooling and vendor management: manage the day-to-day AI tooling estate: select, pilot and manage relationships with AI platforms and vendors, and retire what isn't earning its place, working with the enterprise IT team on infrastructure and security

  • Measurement and reporting: build a simple set of KPIs for adoption, automation impact and ROI, and report progress jointly to the Chief People Officer and Chief AI Officer

What success looks like in year one

  • Everybody at Unity, from Partners to enablement staff, confident and capable using AI well in their day-to-day work

  • Several whole steps or processes genuinely reimagined or removed — not just automated — with visible productivity gains across client delivery and enablement functions

  • Every new and existing employee equipped with practical, role-relevant AI skills, not generic training

  • A clear, shared view with the CAIO and CPO of how roles, judgement and team shape need to evolve as more work moves onto AI and platforms like Weaver

  • AI guardrails followed in practice across the business, without becoming a source of friction

What we're looking for

  • Someone who lives at the frontier: actively building with the latest AI tools themselves and evolving their own approach every few weeks. Come with examples of what you've built — we want to see it, not just hear about it

  • A senior operator with a genuine track record of delivering AI and automation adoption at an organisational level — we're more interested in evidence of real impact than where you've done it before

  • A genuine interest in ways of working, role design and how people actually do their jobs, not just the technology — this is a people and change role as much as a technical one

  • Comfortable building smaller things yourself — prototypes, scripts, workflows — and clear-eyed about when to bring in VP Product and Engineering for shared integrations or production-grade build

  • Comfortable building the operational muscle of a function from scratch, and sequencing what matters most first rather than trying to do everything at once

  • Confident training and influencing Partners and Functional Leaders directly, translating strategy into practical, adopted value

  • A pragmatic operator who executes guardrails without adding bureaucracy — in keeping with Unity's "progress over process" and "light scaffolding" principles

  • Excellent communicator, able to make AI capability accessible and credible to non-technical audiences at every level

How this role fits at Unity

You'll report jointly into the Chief People Officer and the Chief AI Officer — a deliberate dual line, reflecting that this role is as much about capability, learning and ways of working as it is about AI itself. You'll work closely with the Performance & Development Lead so AI capability-building lines up with Unity's wider approach to development and growth, and directly with Partners and Functional Leaders across client teams and enablement functions on automation, adoption and reimagining how work gets done.

With VPs for Product and Engineering, the model is simple: you build and ship smaller things yourself, and bring the team in when something needs shared integrations, scaling or ongoing production support. You'll also work with the enterprise IT team on infrastructure and security.

This is a rare opportunity to shape how a rapidly scaling business drives performance, progression, learning, and culture—and to build People programmes that are genuinely Built Different.

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised

  • Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale

  • Working to resolve complaints without the customer needing to refer to FOS, and applying the learnings from both internal and FOS outcomes to future cases

About the role

Lendable's Payments team transacts money for our UK Loans, AutoLend (motor finance) and Zable (credit card) products: disbursing loans, collecting repayments, refunding customers and reconciling everything against our banking providers.

We're bringing in a recent graduate on a 6-month contract to strengthen the controls around our daily loan funding and to add capacity across payments and partner indemnity recovery. A large part of our AutoLend lending is originated through third-party partners, and you'll own the daily process that verifies funds are flowing correctly through that chain before we release the next day's payments. You'll run that control every day, then use the remaining time to help us make it faster, better evidenced and, where possible, automated.

This is a hands-on operational role and a strong first job in fintech. You don't need finance experience; we'll teach you the payments side. You do need to be numerate, methodical, quick to learn and comfortable being the last line of defence before money leaves the building.

What you'll do

Daily funding controls (core responsibility)

  • Run the daily pre-release checks on partner funding: gather payment evidence from our third-party partners, reconcile it to our disbursal records, and confirm that yesterday's funds reached the intended recipients before today's payments are approved.

  • Hold, query or escalate anything that is missing, late or doesn't reconcile, and document the reason clearly so commercial, operations and risk colleagues can act on it.

  • Keep a full audit trail of every check, exception and release decision so the control is evidenced for internal review and audit.

  • Spot the trends in partner behaviour and payment timing that warrant a closer look, and raise them early.

  • Run periodic verification of partner and payee bank details, and re-verify whenever a partner asks us to change where we pay them.

  • Work with the Payments Manager to onboard more partners onto the control, and to turn the manual check into matching rules, scripts and monitoring that surface only the exceptions.

Payments and finance operations

  • Support day-to-day payment operations: cash allocation of incoming repayments, refunds and returned payments, and reconciliation against our bank and payment providers.

  • Prepare and check payment files for approval, for example, bulk payment files for customer refunds and complaint redress.

  • Pick up Finance Help Desk tickets from other teams: payment traces, refund and redress requests, "has this payment arrived" queries.

 

Partner indemnity recovery

  • Support the colleague who leads our partner indemnity recovery process. Where an agreement is cancelled, unwound or found to have been mis-sold, our partner agreements entitle us to recover amounts from the partner. You'll help validate each case against our records: confirming the agreement status, the amounts paid out and received, and what is contractually recoverable.

  • Prepare and reconcile the recovery figures that go to partners, track invoices raised against amounts received, and chase and resolve queries and shortfalls.

  • Support the unwind process on cancelled agreements: making sure customer refunds, partner recoveries and internal ledger entries all tie back to the same numbers.

  • Help bring the recovery backlog under control and keep an accurate, up-to-date view of what is outstanding by partner.

What we're looking for

Must have

  • A degree (2:1 or above, or equivalent) in a STEM, finance, accounting, economics or other quantitative subject, completed within the last two years.

  • Strong numeracy and comfort working with large volumes of transactional data.

  • Strong attention to detail and healthy scepticism. You can quickly identify when supporting documentation, such as a bank statement, does not fully evidence what it is intended to.

  • Confident with Google Sheets or Excel, including lookups, filters and tidy, checkable working.

  • Clear written communication. You can explain to a non-finance colleague why a payment has been held.

  • Confident dealing with external partners: obtaining documentation promptly and professionally, and politely pushing back where it is incomplete.

  • Comfortable handling sensitive customer, partner and payment data responsibly.

Nice to have

  • Some exposure to Python, SQL or a similar language from your degree, a project or self-study, and an appetite to use it to automate repetitive work. We use Snowflake.

  • An internship, placement or project involving finance, operations or messy real-world data.

  • An interest in payments, lending or how money moves between businesses.

What success looks like at 6 months

  • The daily funding control runs reliably across the agreed partner population with a full evidence trail, and no payment is released without the previous day's funds being evidenced.

  • Exceptions and emerging trends are flagged early, documented and resolved with the right teams.

  • Partner and payee bank details have been verified on the agreed cycle.

  • The partner indemnity recovery backlog has been validated, invoiced where due and is tracked in one accurate, up-to-date view.

  • The funding control is documented end-to-end and materially more automated than when you started.

description:
Our Story
 
Hello there. We’re Zopa.
 
We started our journey back in 2005, building the first ever peer-to-peer lending company. Fast forward to 2020 and we launched Zopa Bank. A bank that listens to what our customers don’t like about finance and does the opposite. We’re redefining what it feels like to work in finance. Our vision for a new era of banking puts people front and centre — we’ve built a business that empowers everyone to aim high, every day, to move finance forward. Find out more about our fantastic offerings at Zopa.com! 
 
We’re incredibly proud of our achievements and none of it would be possible without the amazing team here. It’s not just industry awards we’re winning, we’ve also been named in the top three UK’s Most Loved Workplaces. 
 
If you embrace unconventional challenges, are unafraid to think differently and are driven to make an outsized impact, you’ll thrive here at Zopa, so join us, and make it count. Want to see us in action? Follow us on Instagram @zopalife

The team 

Unsecured Personal Loans is one of Zopa’s largest and most established products, sitting at the heart of the bank’s growth ambitions. As a Product Manager in UPL Growth, you will own a meaningful part of how we originate loans: the decisioning, data and product journeys that determine who we can lend to, how confidently we can make an offer, and how simply customers can access one. 

This is far more than keeping a mature product moving. You will have the space to identify the biggest opportunities to improve conversion, eligibility and growth, then take them from a commercial hypothesis through discovery and delivery into measurable results. That might mean rethinking how we use third-party data, improving a partner journey, or changing the rules and logic behind our lending decisions. 

You will work in a small, ambitious product team alongside three flexible backend engineering teams, with close partnership from Credit Risk, Data Science and First Line Risk. The work is complex, fast-moving and consequential: the decisions you shape will directly influence customer outcomes and the scale of Zopa’s lending business.

The work sits closer to commercial and analytical reasoning than to customer discovery — you will spend as much time interrogating data, sizing opportunities and shaping decisioning logic as you will running user research. If that sounds like the kind of PM work you are drawn to, this role is built for you. 


A day in the life

  • Own a defined area of the UPL growth roadmap, from opportunity sizing through to launch, measurement and iteration. 

  • Turn commercial and customer signals into a clear product strategy, choosing where to focus and what not to pursue. 

  • Shape the origination and decisioning experience, including the rules, journeys and data that sit behind a customer receiving a loan offer. 

  • Lead cross-functional discovery with Engineering, Credit Risk and Data Science to find the most valuable, feasible route to growth. 

  • Develop propositions that give customers greater clarity and confidence before they invest time in a full application. 

  • Make the call on scope and sequencing, balancing customer value, risk, commercial return and engineering effort. 

  • Use data to uncover friction, validate hypotheses and quantify the impact of your work. 

  • Bring new growth ideas into the roadmap, from smarter use of existing data to new external data sources and partner opportunities. 

  • Translate complex lending and technical problems into decisions that senior stakeholders can align behind. 

  • Build, launch and continually improve products that help Zopa move closer to becoming the UK’s leading unsecured lender. 


About you

  • You are analytically strong and comfortable using data to find non-obvious product insight. 

  • You have made product decisions that delivered measurable commercial outcomes. 

  • You can partner closely with engineers through scope and timeline trade-offs. 

  • You approach ambiguous problems with sound judgement and a bias for practical progress. 

  • You communicate clearly with senior stakeholders across technical and risk-focused teams. 

  • You are motivated by growth, efficiency and business impact. 

 

 


Added bonus
  • Experience in lending, consumer credit or related financial products. 

    • Familiarity with originations, underwriting, pricing or servicing. 

    • A quantitative foundation through study or equivalent experience. 

    • Experience in a fast-paced, data-led fintech environment. 

    At Zopa we value flexible ways of working.

    We value face-to-face collaboration and a good work-life balance. This hybrid role requires you to come to our London office 2-3 days a week.

    You'll also have the option of working from abroad for up to 120 days a year!* But no matter where you are, we’ll make sure you’ve got everything you need to thrive, both in your work and home life, from day one.

    *Subject to having the right to work in the country of choice

     

    Diversity Statement

    Zopa is proud to offer a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds leads to better products for our customers and a unique company culture for our people. We are made up of nearly 50 nationalities, have a DE&I forum made up of Zopians wanting to make a difference and we are proud of our culture where everyone can bring their full self to work. Our approach to DE&I is reflected in our hiring process so please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments. 

     

    Our approach to AI in interviews

    At Zopa, AI isn't something we're testing out — it's part of how we work every day. As a proud partner of Jobs 2030, we're committed to building AI fluency across our workforce, and we expect Zopians to use AI as part of how they do their jobs.

An AI-generated answer can't tell us that. What it can do is get in the way of us finding out whether we're the right fit for each other. 

    Technical interviews: it depends on the role. Some technical stages actively welcome AI use, others don't. Your Talent Partner will let you know what's expected at each stage. Where AI is part of the assessment, we'll be interested not just in the outcome, but in how you used it – the tools you chose, your reasoning, and the decisions you made along the way.
